recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No core source fix is needed for FHIR-19439 unless a future final Pharmacy tracker changes the ingredient-strength value set or moves the terminology elsewhere.
issue_request: FHIR-19439 is a Published/Persuasive Pharmacy change request raised against STU3 and applied for R5. It asked how to represent a Medication ingredient whose amount is sufficient quantity; the final resolution was to add a Ratio or CodeableConcept choice to Medication.ingredient.strength with codes such as qs and trace.
initial_application: No current git commit explicitly tagged FHIR-19439 was found. Commit cdb9b154325715da80c5913ec7939955b7d52105 appears to have applied it implicitly by changing Medication.ingredient.strength to strength[x] with Ratio | CodeableConcept and by adding the medication-ingredientstrength CodeSystem/ValueSet with qs and trace.
additional_context: Medication is active and approved in source/fhir.ini. Later FHIR-25122 added Quantity as a third strength[x] type, and FHIR-30879/FHIR-31625 added the distinct Quantity.comparator ad/example family for sufficient quantity to reach a stated total. FHIR-36758 later clarified strength narrative while retaining the same combined type list.
reconciliation: No source change was made because source/medication/structuredefinition-Medication.xml already permits Ratio and CodeableConcept for Medication.ingredient.strength[x], binds the element to ValueSet/medication-ingredientstrength, and the Medication terminology files define qs and trace.
